content: This document serves as an invitation to all stakeholders to initiate or support research that addresses globally identified priority questions in the field of assistive technology. By engaging in such efforts, stakeholders can help bridge the gap between the need for assistive technology and the unmet demand, while also addressing inequities in access that are often determined by wealth rather than actual need. The proposed global research priorities are broad, encompassing numerous thematic areas, each of which includes a variety of relevant research questions. However, the authors have intentionally refrained from listing all possible research questions, allowing researchers and research groups the flexibility to adapt these questions to the specific priorities and needs of their respective settings. While this agenda provides a guiding framework, it is hoped that research in assistive technology will align with the main thematic areas outlined in the document. The global research agenda is not only socially significant but also presents scientific challenges. There is a notable lack of high-quality research and evidence in many of the thematic areas, necessitating the development of new methodologies. Researchers, along with professional and scientific organizations in the field of assistive technology, are encouraged to take on these challenges and collaborate in stimulating and conducting international research as described in this agenda. Additionally, this agenda highlights significant opportunities for industry. The market potential for developing and producing appropriate assistive technology products at affordable costs is immense. The GATE Research Group envisions innovative and exciting collaborations to implement this global priority research agenda, ultimately bringing much-needed assistive products and services to those in need. The document also acknowledges the contributions of over 100 experts who participated in the development of the global assistive technology priority research agenda. These contributions included responses to an online questionnaire, participation in research meetings, and peer reviews. The process was jointly coordinated by several organizations, including the Advancement of Assistive Technology in Europe (AAATE), the Rehabilitation Engineering and Assistive Technology Society of North America (RESNA), Trinity College Dublin, and Zuyd University of Applied Sciences. Financial support was provided by the U.S. Agency for International Development. The agenda emphasizes the importance of addressing critical research questions, such as identifying facilitators and barriers to the use of assistive products and services, developing effective delivery models, monitoring and evaluating assistive technology systems, and promoting policy development to enhance access. These efforts aim to improve access to assistive technology for everyone, everywhere, and to empower individuals in need.
